metadata.title: One Bean for Each of Us
metadata.subtitle: A Week on the Windowsill
metadata.author: Giggle & Snooze
metadata.blurb: Rafi and his cousin Nila sing to their bean pots every morning. When Nila’s seed sprouts first, a notebook helps them spot the little changes as each bean grows in its own time.
metadata.dedication: For everyone who has ever looked twice at a pot of soil.

style_bible.style_prompt_prefix: Original Giggle & Snooze character design: expressive asymmetric poses, rounded bean and crescent shapes, warm playful faces, a small visual joke and a calm cosy atmosphere. Clean contemporary shapes, generous breathing room, one clear story action. Simplify hair, clothing and scenery into broad shapes; include only story-relevant props. Contemporary 2D animation shapes, distinctive silhouettes, expressive eyes, smooth colour fills and restrained soft shading.

characters.name: Rafi
characters.look: Rafi has a round body, warm brown skin, and a single black curl shaped like a comma. He wears a sky-blue shirt and rust-orange shorts, and has a round nose and dark eyes.

characters.name: Nila
characters.look: Nila is tall and slim, with deep brown skin, dark eyes, and black hair in two crescent-shaped puffs. She wears a sunflower-yellow dress over plum leggings and has a gap between her front teeth.

pages.title: Two Pots
pages.text: Rafi planted one bean. His cousin Nila planted one, too. They tucked the beans under the soil like toes under a blanket.
pages.prompt: Rafi and Nila tuck a bean into each of two pots on a low table by a sunny window. Rafi's pot is blue, and Nila's is yellow. A stray crumb of soil sits on Rafi's round nose.

pages.title: The Morning Song
pages.text: Every morning, they sang to their pots. “Up, up, little bean!” On Monday, all they saw was soil.
pages.prompt: Rafi and Nila lean toward the blue and yellow pots with bright singing faces. Both pots show bare soil. A stripe of morning light runs across the tabletop.

pages.title: A Green Hook
pages.text: On Tuesday, Nila saw a green hook in her pot. “Up, up, little bean!” Rafi leaned over his own pot. “I wish mine would come up, too.”
pages.prompt: Nila points to a tiny hooked shoot in the yellow pot. Rafi peers into the blue pot, chin almost level with its rim. Keep the green hook and the bare soil easy to see.

pages.title: Two Pictures
pages.text: “Let’s draw what we see,” said Nila. She drew her green hook. Rafi drew his soil, right down to the little white pebble.
pages.prompt: Rafi and Nila draw in one open notebook, one pot per page. Nila's simple green hook contrasts with Rafi's wide brown patch and carefully outlined pebble. The real pots sit just behind the notebook.

pages.title: Room on the Page
pages.text: On Wednesday, Nila’s hook stood up tall. “Up, up, little bean!” Rafi drew the pebble again. He left room above it, just in case.
pages.prompt: Rafi draws a tiny white pebble low on a fresh notebook page while Nila holds the book steady. Behind them the yellow pot has an upright stem, and the blue pot still holds bare soil and its pebble.

pages.title: A Little Bump
pages.text: On Thursday, the soil in Rafi’s pot had a bump. A little green tip peeked out beside the pebble. “Up, up, little bean!” This time, Rafi sang to something he could see.
pages.prompt: Rafi grins at a green tip breaking through a small mound beside the white pebble in the blue pot. Nila bends close beside him. The yellow pot stands nearby with two small open leaves.

pages.title: Look at Them Now
pages.text: By Sunday, Nila’s bean had leaves as wide as thumbs. Rafi’s bean had two little leaves of its own. They drew both again, and Rafi gave his pebble a spot in the picture, too.
pages.prompt: Rafi and Nila sit shoulder to shoulder at the table with their notebook open to two fresh plant drawings. Show the real plants beside the drawings, with broad leaves in the yellow pot and two smaller leaves in the blue pot. The white pebble appears in the blue pot and in Rafi's drawing.

pages.title: Tomorrow Morning
pages.text: They turned back to the first pictures. “Look how far they’ve come,” said Rafi. Nila tucked a fresh page under the pencil. “Let’s see what they do tomorrow.”
pages.prompt: Rafi looks at the notebook's first spread of a green hook and a patch of soil. Nila holds the corner of the next blank page under a pencil. Both bean plants lean gently into the warm window light behind them.
